blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — healthcare-associated infection outbreak investigation
stem: An infection-prevention team is investigating a cluster of healthcare-associated infections on one unit. Which action is part of the standard outbreak-investigation process?

options.A: Establish a case definition, identify and characterize cases, assess likely exposures or transmission routes, and implement targeted control measures.
options.B: Wait for every case to have an identical organism before beginning case finding or infection-control assessment on the affected unit.
options.C: Close the entire hospital before defining the cases or evaluating likely transmission because broad closure is the routine first control step.
options.D: Delay infection-control measures until the exact source has been proven, even when the investigation has already identified correctable transmission gaps.

rationale: A is correct. CDC's Field Epidemiology Manual describes a stepwise healthcare outbreak investigation that includes establishing case definitions, identifying and counting cases, organizing and analyzing data, developing and testing hypotheses, performing an infection-control assessment, and implementing control measures. CDC also states that control measures should be implemented when deficiencies or gaps are identified and that stopping transmission is the primary goal even if the exact source remains unidentified. B, C, and D delay or overgeneralize control rather than following the standard investigation process.
educational_objective: Recognize core steps in investigating and controlling a healthcare-associated infection outbreak: case definition, case finding and characterization, exposure/transmission assessment, and targeted control measures.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); NCSBN
source_document_title: Healthcare Settings — The CDC Field Epidemiology Manual; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual healthcare-settings chapter dated August 8, 2024 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Healthcare Settings, Field Investigation Steps 4-9: establish case definition(s); identify/count cases; organize data by person/place/time/size; targeted observations and data collection; formulate/test hypotheses; infection-control assessment and implementation of control measures. Step 9.2: implement control measures as soon as deficiencies/gaps are identified; primary goal is to stop transmission even when the specific source remains unidentified.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC field-epidemiology guidance directly supports case definition, case finding, descriptive/analytic assessment, infection-control assessment, and targeted intervention without waiting for perfect source certainty.

option_audit.A: Correct; accurately summarizes CDC's standard healthcare-outbreak investigation and control sequence.
option_audit.B: Plausible microbiologic-certainty misconception but case finding and assessment do not wait for identical organisms in every case.
option_audit.C: Plausible aggressive-control response but whole-hospital closure is not the routine first step before case definition and assessment.
option_audit.D: Plausible causality-first misconception but CDC recommends acting on identified infection-control gaps before exact source certainty when needed.

cueing_audit.answer_length: All options are comparable in detail and professional tone; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
